description: bitFlyer FX_BTC_JPY public WS feed, extracted into compact daily CSVs by scripts/extract_tape.py from the raw recordings in data/ws/ (data/ws is not itself covered here; it is the raw jsonl.gz WS capture, kept as the immutable original — see known_defects).
source: bitFlyer public WebSocket (lightning_ticker_FX_BTC_JPY, lightning_executions_FX_BTC_JPY, lightning_board_FX_BTC_JPY / _snapshot_FX_BTC_JPY), recorded by the resident WS collector into data/ws/*.jsonl.gz, then extracted by scripts/extract_tape.py
retention: bitFlyer's own public REST history is 31 days; these extracted daily CSVs are the long-term substitute and are kept indefinitely once written (never regenerated in a way that drops old days).

ts.meaning: trade/quote time reported by the EXCHANGE (lightning_ticker message's own `timestamp` field), not our receipt time
ts.unit: ISO-8601, sub-second precision as bitFlyer sends it
ts.notes: consecutive rows with an identical (best_bid, best_ask, best_bid_size, best_ask_size) quadruple are DROPPED by extract_tape.py (dedup) -- gaps between rows are not necessarily missing data, they can be an unchanged quote

ts.meaning: TRADE time reported by the exchange (`exec_date` from the lightning_executions message)
ts.unit: ISO-8601, sub-second precision as bitFlyer sends it
ts.notes: this is execution/trade time, matching the `ts` = 約定時刻 half of the t/ts distinction this schema set exists to pin down

ts.meaning: OUR receipt/collection time (`rts`, the WS recorder's local wall clock when the line was written), truncated to whole seconds -- NOT an exchange-reported time. The order book is reconstructed in memory from snapshot+diff messages, which individually carry no timestamp of their own; one row is emitted per second holding that second's LAST book state.
ts.tz: UTC (recorder host clock, NTP-synced, not verified here)
ts.notes: THIS IS THE t = 収集時刻 (collection time) HALF of the known t/ts mixup flagged in docs/DATA_GOVERNANCE_PLAN.md section 1 -- both this file and ticker/executions above name their time column `ts`, but board_top5's `ts` is collection time while ticker/executions' `ts` is exchange/trade time. Do not assume a shared meaning for `ts` across files in this dataset without checking which file it is.

bid_px_1..5.notes: blank cell if book has fewer than 5 levels on that side at that second

bid_sz_1..5.meaning: size at each bid level, same order as bid_px_*

ask_px_1..5.notes: blank cell if book has fewer than 5 levels on that side at that second

ask_sz_1..5.meaning: size at each ask level, same order as ask_px_*

known_defects: t/ts column-meaning mixup risk: `ts` means exchange trade time in executions_*.csv.gz and ticker_*.csv.gz, but means our own WS receipt time (from `rts`) in board_top5_*.csv.gz. Confirmed by reading scripts/extract_tape.py (2026-09-05); this is the concrete instance behind the general t=collection-time / ts=trade-time warning in docs/DATA_GOVERNANCE_PLAN.md section 1.

extract_tape.py stops at the first line in a data/ws/*.jsonl.gz file that fails to parse (torn write / truncated gzip tail) and keeps only what parsed before that point -- a daily CSV can therefore end mid-day with no error raised. Cross-check against data/ws/ (or its listing, paper_logs/ws_listing.txt) coverage before assuming a day is complete.

board_top5 reconstruction requires replaying a file from its first line to rebuild in-memory book state; diffs seen before the first snapshot on a file are dropped as unusable, so book state (and thus every ts row) can be briefly wrong or sparse right after a WS (re)connect.

raw WS recordings in data/ws/*.jsonl.gz are the original source of everything in this schema and are NEVER deleted, even after extraction -- treat data/tape/ and paper_logs/tape/ as a derived, re-generatable convenience, not the primary record.
